def find_reversal(cards):
    n = len(cards)
    i = 0
    while i + 1 < n and cards[i] <= cards[i + 1]:
        i += 1
    
    if i == n - 1:
        return "impossible"
    
    j = i + 1
    while j + 1 < n and cards[j] <= cards[j + 1]:
        j += 1
    
    temp = cards[:i] + cards[i:j+1][::-1] + cards[j+1:]
    
    k = 0
    while k + 1 < n and temp[k] <= temp[k + 1]:
        k += 1
    
    if k == n - 1:
        return i + 1, j + 1
    
    return "impossible"

def find_reversal_indices(cards):
    n = len(cards)
    first, last = None, None
    
    # Find the first index where the current card is less than the previous card
    for i in range(1, n):
        if cards[i] < cards[i - 1]:
            first = i
            break
    
    # If no such index is found, the array is already sorted
    if first is None:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Find the last index where the current card is less than the next card
    for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        if cards[i] > cards[i + 1]:
            last = i
            break
    
    # Check if reversing the subarray from first to last makes the array sorted
    reversed_subarray = cards[first:last+1][::-1]
    if cards[:first] + reversed_subarray + cards[last+1:] == sorted(cards):
        return f"{first+1} {last+1}"
    else:
        return "impossible"

def reverse_subarray_to_sort(cards):
    n = len(cards)
    start, end = -1, -1
    
    # Find the first place where the array is not sorted
    for i in range(1, n):
        if cards[i] < cards[i - 1]:
            start = i - 1
            break
    
    # If the array is already sorted
    if start == -1:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Continue finding the last place where the array is not sorted
    for j in range(start + 1, n):
        if cards[j] < cards[j - 1]:
            end = j
            break
    
    # Reverse the subarray [start:end+1]
    while start < end:
        cards[start], cards[end] = cards[end], cards[start]
        start += 1
        end -= 1
    
    # Check if the array is sorted after reversing
    for i in range(1, n):
        if cards[i] < cards[i - 1]:
            return "impossible"
    
    # Return the 1-based index range
    return f"{start + 1} {end + 1}"

def reverse_subarray_to_sort(cards):
    n = len(cards)
    if n < 2:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Find the first pair where the sequence breaks the non-decreasing property
    start = None
    for i in range(1, n):
        if cards[i] < cards[i - 1]:
            start = i - 1
            break
    
    if start is None:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Find the last pair where the sequence breaks the non-decreasing property
    end = None
    for i in range(start + 1, n):
        if cards[i] < cards[i - 1]:
            end = i
            break
    
    if end is None or end == n - 1:
        end = n
    
    # Check if reversing the subarray [start:end+1] will sort the array
    reversed_subarray = cards[start:end]
    reversed_subarray.reverse()
    if start > 0 and cards[start - 1] > reversed_subarray[-1]:
        return "impossible"
    if end < n and reversed_subarray[0] > cards[end]:
        return "impossible"
    if end == n - 1 and start > 0 and cards[start - 1] > cards[end]:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Verify if the rest of the array is sorted
    for i in range(end + 1, n):
        if cards[i] < cards[i - 1]:
            return "impossible"
    
    return f"{start + 1} {end}"

    start = -1

    # Find the first element that breaks the non-decreasing order
    for i in range(1, n):
        if cards[i] < cards[i - 1]:
            start = i - 1
            break
    
    # If the entire array is already sorted
    if start == -1:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Continue finding the last element that breaks the non-decreasing order
    for i in range(start + 1, n):
        if cards[i] >= cards[start]:
            end = i
        else:
            end = i - 1
            break
    
    # Check if reversing this subarray sorts the array
    if start == 0 and end == n - 1 and cards[end] <= cards[0]:
        return f"{start + 1} {end + 1}"
    
    # Verify the reversal fixes the sequence
    reversed_subarray = cards[start:end+1][::-1]
    temp_cards = cards[:start] + reversed_subarray + cards[end+1:]
    
    if temp_cards == sorted(temp_cards):
        return f"{start + 1} {end + 1}"
    
    return "impossible"

def find_reversal_subarray(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    if n == 1:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Find the first place where nums[i] > nums[i+1]
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 and nums[i] <= nums[i + 1]:
        i += 1
    
    # If the entire array is already sorted, no need to reverse
    if i == n - 1:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Find the second place where nums[j] < nums[j-1]
    j = n - 1
    while j > 0 and nums[j] >= nums[j - 1]:
        j -= 1
    
    # Check if reversing nums[i:j+1] will sort the array
    temp = nums[:]
    temp[i:j+1] = reversed(temp[i:j+1])
    if temp == sorted(temp):
        return [i + 1, j + 1]
    
    return "impossible"

        return "impossible"

    for j in range(left + 1, n):

            right = j - 1

    if all(cards[i] <= cards[i + 1] for i in range(left, right)) and \
       (left == 0 or cards[left] >= cards[right + 1]) and \

    left = -1
    right = -1
    
    # Find the first pair where arr[i] > arr[i+1]
    for i in range(n - 1):
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1]:
            left = i
            break
    
    # If no such pair is found, the array is already sorted
    if left == -1:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Find the second pair where arr[i] < arr[i+1]
    for j in range(left + 1, n - 1):
        if arr[j] < arr[j + 1]:
            right = j
            break
    
    # Reverse the identified subarray
    while left < right:
        arr[left], arr[right] = arr[right], arr[left]
        left += 1
        right -= 1
    
    # Verify if the array is sorted
    for k in range(n - 1):
        if arr[k] > arr[k + 1]:
            return "impossible"
    
    # Return the result
    return f"{left + 1} {right + 1}"

    if i == n - 1:
        return "impossible"
    
    j = i

        j += 1
    
    if j == n - 1 and cards[i] >= cards[0]:
        return f"{i + 1} {j + 1}"

def reverse_subarray_to_sort(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    start = -1
    end = -1
    
    # Traverse the array from left to right to find the first pair where arr[i] > arr[i + 1]
    for i in range(n - 1):
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1]:
            start = i
            break
    
    # If no such pair is found, the array is already sorted
    if start == -1:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Traverse the array from right to left to find the last pair where arr[j - 1] > arr[j]
    for j in range(n - 1, 0, -1):
        if arr[j - 1] > arr[j]:
            end = j
            break
    
    # Reverse the subarray from start to end
    arr[start:end+1] = reversed(arr[start:end+1])
    
    # Check if the array is sorted after reversing
    for k in range(n - 1):
        if arr[k] > arr[k + 1]:
            return "impossible"
    
    return f"{start + 1} {end}"

def reverse_subarray_to_sort(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    first_mismatch = None
    last_mismatch = None
    
    # Find the first point where the array is not sorted in ascending order
    for i in range(1, n):
        if arr[i] < arr[i - 1]:
            if first_mismatch is None:
                first_mismatch = i
            else:
                return "impossible"
    
    # If the array is already sorted
    if first_mismatch is None:
        return "impossible"
    
    # Find the second point where the array is not sorted in ascending order
    for i in range(first_mismatch + 1, n):
        if arr[i] > arr[first_mismatch - 1]:
            last_mismatch = i
    
    # Check if reversing the subarray [first_mismatch-1, last_mismatch] sorts the array
    reversed_subarray = arr[first_mismatch-1:last_mismatch+1][::-1]
    expected_array = arr[:first_mismatch-1] + reversed_subarray + arr[last_mismatch+1:]
    
    for i in range(1, n):
        if expected_array[i] < expected_array[i - 1]:
            return "impossible"
    
    return f"{first_mismatch} {last_mismatch}"
